bull_bear.body:
- Indigenous manufacturing and import-substitution positioning across telecom, railways, defence, utilities and smart infrastructure
- Installed credibility with premier Indian research and defence institutions - products stated to be trusted by DRDO and ISRO
- In-house design and manufacture across a broad fiber optic instrument range (splicing, OTDR, power metering, fault location, marking) rather than a single product line
- TSEC-certified RFMS and RFTS platforms enabling access to large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet
- State-of-the-art in-house testing laboratory established to simulate field conditions
- Collaboration with a US-based OEM specialising in RF technologies for RF-over-Fiber design and development
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Liquidity strain evidenced by chronic non-payment of undisputed statutory dues — The statutory auditors drew an Emphasis of Matter that the Company is irregular in payment of PF, TDS, PT, Sales Tax and Service Tax, with total outstanding statutory dues of Rs. 136.76 Lakhs as on 31 March 2026, and that arrears remained outstanding beyond six months from when they became payable. The Board attributes this to temporary cash flow constraints and says regularisation will be phased and dependent on cash flow improvement - making working-capital availability a structural constraint on operations and on the Company's ability to fund its stated expansion.
- Competition from well-established players as the Company enters new product domains — Management flags that entering new domains (Telecom Network Solutions, defence RF) brings direct competition with entrenched incumbents, and that success hinges on differentiating the offering and demonstrating value. Separately, tough competition in the testing-equipment space is cited as able to squeeze prices and cut into profits - a direct margin risk given the Company's stated need for margin recovery.
- Regulatory and compliance complexity across diverse frameworks and standards — Management identifies adherence to diverse regulatory frameworks and local standards as a critical priority; while T&M equipment has TEC approval, maintaining ongoing compliance across all regions is essential to avoid disruptions. Evolving regulations and standards are separately flagged as compliance risks that may demand substantial investment in product adaptation.
- Supply chain and logistics vulnerability — Management states global supply-chain fluctuations and logistical constraints pose potential risks to timely product delivery, and cites supply chain variability as one factor that may influence near-term performance. For a hardware manufacturer dependent on imported RF and optical components this is a delivery- and cost-side exposure.
- Execution risk on the defence and new-product diversification, which is early stage and unproven — The pivot into defence (indigenous SSPA, RF cable assemblies, RF-over-Fiber) and into Telecom Network Solutions is the stated basis for revenue diversification and margin recovery, but management itself describes these initiatives as currently in early stages, with medium-term access to defence, space and satellite programmes only 'expected'. The RFID target and BharatNet participation are explicitly made subject to timely client adoption and system integration.
- Rapid technological obsolescence in network testing equipment — Management flags the fast pace of technological change as a threat, requiring constant innovation to keep up with evolving network technologies (5G, FTTH, SDN, next-generation optical). Failure to keep pace would erode the T&M franchise that still forms the core of the business.
- Pattern of listing-regulation and statutory filing lapses indicating weak compliance infrastructure — The Secretarial Auditor raised nine observations for FY 2025-26, including delayed submission of board-meeting outcomes beyond the 30-minute timeline, a missing QR code in the newspaper publication of results, non-submission of the statement of utilisation of issue proceeds for warrant-conversion allotments under Regulation 32(1), a non-filed FY 2024-25 FLA Return, MCA filings made with additional fees and e-forms still pending, and annexures referenced in the prior year's Board Report but never attached. The Board attributes all to inadvertence, but the volume indicates a structural governance/compliance-capacity weakness.
- Cyclical exposure to telecom operator capital spending — Management flags that a weakened economic climate can prompt telecom providers to scale back investments, negatively impacting the market for testing equipment. Combined with the Company's concentration in telecom and public-sector/government customers, demand is tied to third-party infrastructure capex cycles and programme timing.

business.body: Telogica designs and manufactures fiber optic instruments and telecommunication solutions - splicing machines, OTDRs, laser sources, optical power meters, cable route tracers, cable fault locators and RFID markers/marker locators - used for installation, maintenance and troubleshooting of fiber optic networks. It sells to telecom service providers, government and public sector undertakings, defence establishments, utilities, research institutions and enterprise customers, and collaborates with global technology partners for supply, integration and deployment of advanced communication technologies. During FY 2025-26 the Company extended beyond its established T&M range into Telecom Network Solutions and into defence-oriented RF products including Solid-State Power Amplifiers and RF-over-Fiber systems.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Fiber optic test & measurement:** Fiber Splicing Machines, Optical Time Domain Reflectometers (OTDR), Laser Sources, Optical Power Meters, Cable Route Tracers, Cable Fault Locators, Markers (Active RFID and Passive) and Marker Locators
- **Telecom Network Solutions:** Digital Earthing Device, FXS Gateway (carrier-grade VoIP gateway), Optimux (Optical Multiplexer), RFID Markers, RFID Locators, RFMS and RFTS platforms
- **Defence / RF:** Solid-State Power Amplifiers (SSPA), DC to 40 GHz, RF Cable Assemblies, RF-over-Fiber solutions (10 kHz to 70 GHz), Programmable delay line systems (30 MHz to 40 GHz), Polarization-Maintaining (PM) fiber solutions
- **Optical networks (under development):** EDFA amplifiers, GPS-integrated cable route racers

outlook.body:
- Evolve from a Testing & Measuring (T&M) equipment maker into a comprehensive Telecom Solutions provider, via new Telecom Network Solutions products (Digital Earthing Device, FXS Gateway, Optimux)
- Enter and build out the defence vertical, centred on an indigenous Solid-State Power Amplifier (DC-40 GHz), RF cable assemblies and RF-over-Fiber solutions
- Pursue indigenous manufacturing and import substitution across telecom, railways, defence, utilities and smart infrastructure
- Deepen presence in optical networking through development of EDFA amplifiers for long-haul fiber infrastructure
- Scale the RFID Marker and Locator business and leverage TSEC-certified RFMS/RFTS platforms to participate in large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet
- Diversify the revenue base to reduce dependence on the traditional telecom testing equipment market
- Restore margins through an expanded product mix weighted toward higher-value defence and telecom solutions offerings, alongside operational efficiency
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Telogica's FY 2025-26 expansion is product- and capability-led rather than a rupee-quantified plant programme. The Company extended its established Testing & Measuring range into Telecom Network Solutions with three newly introduced products - a Digital Earthing Device for continuous monitoring of earthing systems, an FXS Gateway (carrier-grade VoIP gateway integrating analog telephones with IP networks) and Optimux, an optical multiplexer for voice, data and Ethernet over fiber - and added RFID Markers and RFID Locators to the portfolio. It obtained TSEC Certification for RFMS and RFTS, enabling participation in major national projects including BharatNet, and established a state-of-the-art testing laboratory to simulate field conditions. Separately the Company is expanding into the defence vertical, venturing into production of Solid-State Power Amplifiers spanning DC to 40 GHz (power up to a few kW) for communication, radar, electronic warfare and satellite applications, together with RF cable assemblies and, in collaboration with a US-based OEM, RF-over-Fiber solutions covering 10 kHz to 70 GHz in compact-module, rackmount and mainframe-based configurations, plus programmable delay lines from 30 MHz to 40 GHz. Products still under development include a cost-effective Cable Route Tracer, internally produced GPS-integrated cable route racers, the indigenous SSPA, and EDFA amplifiers intended to deepen the Company's presence in long-haul optical networking. The annual report attaches no commissioning date, ramp schedule or capital outlay to any of these initiatives, and management describes the defence initiatives as currently in early stages.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Ongoing 5G rollout is fuelling demand for advanced testing solutions that validate performance, latency and reliability
- Growing demand for fiber-to-the-home and next-generation optical networks is expected to sustain demand for the core T&M product range
- Proliferation of IoT and Machine-to-Machine devices is creating a need for specialised testing tools
- The shift toward network virtualization and Software-Defined Networking opens the market for adaptable testing platforms
- Rising network-security concerns are growing the market for cybersecurity testing equipment
- Integration of automation and artificial intelligence into testing workflows is improving efficiency and enabling intelligent analysis of complex network behaviour
- Expansion into Telecom Network Solutions is expected to capture a larger share of wallet from existing telecom customers while opening new revenue streams
- Defence, space and satellite communication programmes are expected to open up over the medium term via the indigenous SSPA and RF-over-Fiber collaboration, though management states these initiatives are currently in early stages
- Participation in large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet, via TSEC-certified RFMS/RFTS and RFID products, is anticipated to be an incremental growth driver, subject to timely client adoption and system integration
- Near-term performance may continue to be influenced by competitive pricing pressure, regulatory compliance requirements and supply chain variability

deepdive.thesis: Telogica Limited is a Hyderabad-based manufacturer of fiber optic test-and-measurement instruments and telecom network solutions, now extending into defence RF and telecom-infrastructure products.

open.item: The Company is targeting sale of 100,000 RFID Markers during the financial year.
The Company is targeting sale of 200 RFID Locators during the financial year.
A target of 100,000 RFID Markers and 200 RFID Locators for the coming year, expected to make this an incremental growth driver.
Development of an indigenous Solid-State Power Amplifier operating from DC to 40 GHz for defence and high-frequency communication applications, as part of the Company's entry into the defence sector.
The Company is developing a cost-effective Cable Route Tracer, including GPS-integrated cable route racers produced internally.
Telogica is developing EDFA amplifiers to deepen its presence in the optical networking space for long-haul fiber infrastructure.

The Board has committed to regularising outstanding undisputed statutory dues (Provident Fund, Sales Tax, TDS, Professional Tax and TCS) at the earliest, in a phased manner, based on improvement in the Company's cash flow position - a trackable remediation promise arising from an auditor observation.

The Company is in the process of compiling the statement of utilisation of issue proceeds / statement of deviation for equity shares allotted on conversion of warrants (October-November 2025) and will submit it to the Stock Exchange at the earliest, and is taking steps to file the pending FLA Return for FY 2024-25.
The Company intends to evolve into a comprehensive Telecom Solutions provider through its newly introduced Digital Earthing Device, FXS Gateway and Optimux products.

Entry into the defence sector remains a key strategic priority, expected to open access to defence, space and satellite communication programmes over the medium term and to diversify the revenue base.

Following moderation in profitability during FY 2025-26, the Company states it remains focused on operational efficiency and margin recovery through its expanded product mix and higher-value defence and telecom solutions offerings.
The Company is venturing into production of indigenous Solid-State Power Amplifiers with a frequency range from DC to 40 GHz for defence and high-frequency communication applications.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Telogica Limited is a Hyderabad-based manufacturer of fiber optic test-and-measurement instruments and telecom network solutions, now extending into defence RF and telecom-infrastructure products.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Telogica designs and manufactures fiber optic instruments and telecommunication solutions - splicing machines, OTDRs, laser sources, optical power meters, cable route tracers, cable fault locators and RFID markers/marker locators - used for installation, maintenance and troubleshooting of fiber optic networks. It sells to telecom service providers, government and public sector undertakings, defence establishments, utilities, research institutions and enterprise customers, and collaborates with global technology partners for supply, integration and deployment of advanced communication technologies. During FY 2025-26 the Company extended beyond its established T&M range into Telecom Network Solutions and into defence-oriented RF products including Solid-State Power Amplifiers and RF-over-Fiber systems.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fiber optic test & measurement:** Fiber Splicing Machines, Optical Time Domain Reflectometers (OTDR), Laser Sources, Optical Power Meters, Cable Route Tracers, Cable Fault Locators, Markers (Active RFID and Passive) and Marker Locators
- **Telecom Network Solutions:** Digital Earthing Device, FXS Gateway (carrier-grade VoIP gateway), Optimux (Optical Multiplexer), RFID Markers, RFID Locators, RFMS and RFTS platforms
- **Defence / RF:** Solid-State Power Amplifiers (SSPA), DC to 40 GHz, RF Cable Assemblies, RF-over-Fiber solutions (10 kHz to 70 GHz), Programmable delay line systems (30 MHz to 40 GHz), Polarization-Maintaining (PM) fiber solutions
- **Optical networks (under development):** EDFA amplifiers, GPS-integrated cable route racers

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Ongoing 5G rollout is fuelling demand for advanced testing solutions that validate performance, latency and reliability
- Growing demand for fiber-to-the-home and next-generation optical networks is expected to sustain demand for the core T&M product range
- Proliferation of IoT and Machine-to-Machine devices is creating a need for specialised testing tools
- The shift toward network virtualization and Software-Defined Networking opens the market for adaptable testing platforms
- Rising network-security concerns are growing the market for cybersecurity testing equipment
- Integration of automation and artificial intelligence into testing workflows is improving efficiency and enabling intelligent analysis of complex network behaviour
- Expansion into Telecom Network Solutions is expected to capture a larger share of wallet from existing telecom customers while opening new revenue streams
- Defence, space and satellite communication programmes are expected to open up over the medium term via the indigenous SSPA and RF-over-Fiber collaboration, though management states these initiatives are currently in early stages
- Participation in large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet, via TSEC-certified RFMS/RFTS and RFID products, is anticipated to be an incremental growth driver, subject to timely client adoption and system integration
- Near-term performance may continue to be influenced by competitive pricing pressure, regulatory compliance requirements and supply chain variability

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Evolve from a Testing & Measuring (T&M) equipment maker into a comprehensive Telecom Solutions provider, via new Telecom Network Solutions products (Digital Earthing Device, FXS Gateway, Optimux)
- Enter and build out the defence vertical, centred on an indigenous Solid-State Power Amplifier (DC-40 GHz), RF cable assemblies and RF-over-Fiber solutions
- Pursue indigenous manufacturing and import substitution across telecom, railways, defence, utilities and smart infrastructure
- Deepen presence in optical networking through development of EDFA amplifiers for long-haul fiber infrastructure
- Scale the RFID Marker and Locator business and leverage TSEC-certified RFMS/RFTS platforms to participate in large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet
- Diversify the revenue base to reduce dependence on the traditional telecom testing equipment market
- Restore margins through an expanded product mix weighted toward higher-value defence and telecom solutions offerings, alongside operational efficiency

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Telogica's FY 2025-26 expansion is product- and capability-led rather than a rupee-quantified plant programme. The Company extended its established Testing & Measuring range into Telecom Network Solutions with three newly introduced products - a Digital Earthing Device for continuous monitoring of earthing systems, an FXS Gateway (carrier-grade VoIP gateway integrating analog telephones with IP networks) and Optimux, an optical multiplexer for voice, data and Ethernet over fiber - and added RFID Markers and RFID Locators to the portfolio. It obtained TSEC Certification for RFMS and RFTS, enabling participation in major national projects including BharatNet, and established a state-of-the-art testing laboratory to simulate field conditions. Separately the Company is expanding into the defence vertical, venturing into production of Solid-State Power Amplifiers spanning DC to 40 GHz (power up to a few kW) for communication, radar, electronic warfare and satellite applications, together with RF cable assemblies and, in collaboration with a US-based OEM, RF-over-Fiber solutions covering 10 kHz to 70 GHz in compact-module, rackmount and mainframe-based configurations, plus programmable delay lines from 30 MHz to 40 GHz. Products still under development include a cost-effective Cable Route Tracer, internally produced GPS-integrated cable route racers, the indigenous SSPA, and EDFA amplifiers intended to deepen the Company's presence in long-haul optical networking. The annual report attaches no commissioning date, ramp schedule or capital outlay to any of these initiatives, and management describes the defence initiatives as currently in early stages.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Indigenous manufacturing and import-substitution positioning across telecom, railways, defence, utilities and smart infrastructure
- Installed credibility with premier Indian research and defence institutions - products stated to be trusted by DRDO and ISRO
- In-house design and manufacture across a broad fiber optic instrument range (splicing, OTDR, power metering, fault location, marking) rather than a single product line
- TSEC-certified RFMS and RFTS platforms enabling access to large national infrastructure programmes such as BharatNet
- State-of-the-art in-house testing laboratory established to simulate field conditions
- Collaboration with a US-based OEM specialising in RF technologies for RF-over-Fiber design and development

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Liquidity strain evidenced by chronic non-payment of undisputed statutory dues — The statutory auditors drew an Emphasis of Matter that the Company is irregular in payment of PF, TDS, PT, Sales Tax and Service Tax, with total outstanding statutory dues of Rs. 136.76 Lakhs as on 31 March 2026, and that arrears remained outstanding beyond six months from when they became payable. The Board attributes this to temporary cash flow constraints and says regularisation will be phased and dependent on cash flow improvement - making working-capital availability a structural constraint on operations and on the Company's ability to fund its stated expansion.
- Competition from well-established players as the Company enters new product domains — Management flags that entering new domains (Telecom Network Solutions, defence RF) brings direct competition with entrenched incumbents, and that success hinges on differentiating the offering and demonstrating value. Separately, tough competition in the testing-equipment space is cited as able to squeeze prices and cut into profits - a direct margin risk given the Company's stated need for margin recovery.
- Regulatory and compliance complexity across diverse frameworks and standards — Management identifies adherence to diverse regulatory frameworks and local standards as a critical priority; while T&M equipment has TEC approval, maintaining ongoing compliance across all regions is essential to avoid disruptions. Evolving regulations and standards are separately flagged as compliance risks that may demand substantial investment in product adaptation.
- Supply chain and logistics vulnerability — Management states global supply-chain fluctuations and logistical constraints pose potential risks to timely product delivery, and cites supply chain variability as one factor that may influence near-term performance. For a hardware manufacturer dependent on imported RF and optical components this is a delivery- and cost-side exposure.
- Execution risk on the defence and new-product diversification, which is early stage and unproven — The pivot into defence (indigenous SSPA, RF cable assemblies, RF-over-Fiber) and into Telecom Network Solutions is the stated basis for revenue diversification and margin recovery, but management itself describes these initiatives as currently in early stages, with medium-term access to defence, space and satellite programmes only 'expected'. The RFID target and BharatNet participation are explicitly made subject to timely client adoption and system integration.
- Rapid technological obsolescence in network testing equipment — Management flags the fast pace of technological change as a threat, requiring constant innovation to keep up with evolving network technologies (5G, FTTH, SDN, next-generation optical). Failure to keep pace would erode the T&M franchise that still forms the core of the business.
- Pattern of listing-regulation and statutory filing lapses indicating weak compliance infrastructure — The Secretarial Auditor raised nine observations for FY 2025-26, including delayed submission of board-meeting outcomes beyond the 30-minute timeline, a missing QR code in the newspaper publication of results, non-submission of the statement of utilisation of issue proceeds for warrant-conversion allotments under Regulation 32(1), a non-filed FY 2024-25 FLA Return, MCA filings made with additional fees and e-forms still pending, and annexures referenced in the prior year's Board Report but never attached. The Board attributes all to inadvertence, but the volume indicates a structural governance/compliance-capacity weakness.
- Cyclical exposure to telecom operator capital spending — Management flags that a weakened economic climate can prompt telecom providers to scale back investments, negatively impacting the market for testing equipment. Combined with the Company's concentration in telecom and public-sector/government customers, demand is tied to third-party infrastructure capex cycles and programme timing.
